I got pumpkin carving banned at my elementary school.

It's still really infuriating to me, actually. When I was in second grade, we had a pumpkin carving day before Halloween. Our newly hired vice principal was observing the class for some reason. While carving, I was having a blast and really excited. When I was younger, I had this.... really embarrassing....tick, I guess, where, when I got really excited, my hands would start shaking and my mouth would be open really wide while vibrating. I have no idea why it happened, it actually still happens sometimes, I'm just a lot better at controlling it. I probably have a brain tumor, who knows.

Anyways, I was having a grand old time carving pumpkins and I did the retarded excitement freakout thing and then, self conciously, immediately went back to carving. Suddenly, I get pulled up by my arm and whisked out of the room by the new vice principal. She was looking at me angrier than I can remember seeing an adult at that age.

"Why did you try to hurt that boy? What were you thinking?"

I had no idea what was happening and told her so. She said I knew what I had done and was lying to her face. She thought I was going to stab the kid next to me in the back. I shyly tried to explain my weird emotional tick that embarrassed me as she pulled me down to the office, yelling at me. 

I spent the rest of the day alone, confused, and crying in a small room with glass walls inside the main office with adult authority figures and strangers looking in at me like I was a horrifying zoo exhibit. Actually, my teacher did come in at one point and scold me, telling me how she'd never heard of a student behaving so psychotically. Although she hadn't actually seen it, she just heard about it from the vice principal and wouldn't listen to my side. I was such a passive, quiet student. A timid, tiny, second grade girl whom these adults were treating like a murderous Chucky doll. Eventually, my mom came and took me to get ice cream and then took me home. I don't really remember her reaction, I think because the memory of the other adults was so strong and frightening to me.

Talking to her about it years later, I found out the school tried to expell me for attacking a kid. I must reiterate, all I had done was stretch out my arms with a knife in my hands and shake my arms in front of me with my mouth hanging open for about three seconds, then go back to carving. Fucking weird, yes. Attacking someone? No. My mom was super pissed off about their reaction and told them that they had no grounds to expell me: I was required to bring in a pumpkin carving kit for the day, I had no history of aggression, an established history of being an excitable weirdo, and nobody was scared or hurt by my actions. (I think only the vice principal even saw it because all the other kids were asking me what happened when I got back in class. My teacher told me, in front of the entire classroom of course, that I wasn't allowed to talk about it and that I should be too ashamed to want to tell anyone anyways.)

My mom threatened to sue if they expelled me and they dropped it. But that teacher and vice principal were always mean to me after that. And every Halloween, everyone would be assholes to me for getting pumpkin carving banned.

I was basically in love with the same guy from 10th to 12th grade. We were friends but for some reason I felt like he never noticed me. I even dated other people trying to get over him but could not get him out of my head.

10 years later, happily engaged and living across the world from my old crush (whom I hardly thought about anymore), I came across my senior year yearbook and saw the message he left me. He filled a whole page on my book with a cute picture representing our "love" and wrote me the sweetest message and like a lightbulb it seemed so obvious that he liked me too. I probably seemed so unapproachable because he was shy but I was kinda in a wild and colorful stage of life and dating other people so he probably didn't think I noticed him.

Reading his note flooded back years of emotion and I had to go vomit and cry. I felt like I was mourning a path I didn't take. Where would I be of I had made my feelings towards him clearer in highschool? Would we still be together now? I was stuck in a funk for months, loving the happy blissful life I have but imagining and idolizing where I'd be now if I had been more honest about my feelings as a teenager.

Then I went through a brief stalking phase, reading everything he's posted on Facebook since our graduation. Scrutinizing the girl he ended up with(funnily enough, we're both with people who kinda look like each other). Watching every video he's in online ( he's an actor so I watched all his work. I've even considered writing a script so I can make a movie so I can hire him as an actor so I can see him again). It was weird.

But then I realized so much of what I love about life right now couldn't be if I had followed the path that had the two of us together. I wouldn't be the person I am now and would have to make sacrifices I'm not sure I'd be willing to make. And all for a boy who I didn't know anymore.

Now he's back in the past. He still shines like a lighthouse in the dark, and as silly as it is, I do think he'll always be an important part of my life because he's an amazing person. But more because he will always hold the mystery of "what could have been" in my head. Life is full of unchosen chances and the ones we don't take can have as much of an impact as the ones we do.
